definitions: present participle of use
to know why or how something happens or works :
to know how someone feels or why someone behaves in a particular way:
to think , especially wrongly , that someone means or something is about a particular thing:
When two people understand one another, they both know what the other means and wants and they have an agreement :
to know or realize something because you have been told it:
examples: She explained the whole idea again, but I still didn't understand.
Is there anyone here who understands Arabic ?
I think he was calling from a club - it was so noisy , I couldn't understand a word he said.
We still don't fully understand how the brain works .
My wife doesn't understand me.
Sometimes I don't understand James.

definitions: in or to a position below or lower than something else , often so that one thing covers the other:
If a piece of land is under a particular type of plant , that plant is growing on the whole of that area :
If a book , article , or piece of information is under a particular title , you can find it below or following that title in a list , book , library , etc.:
less than:
happening during, as a result of, or according to a particular situation , event , rule , etc.:
examples: He hid under the bed .
In AD 79 the city of Pompei was buried under a layer of ash seven metres deep .
She put the thermometer under my tongue .
She was holding a folder under her arm (= between her upper arm and the side of her body )
They stood under a tree (= below its branches )
The main fields are under wheat .

definitions: a place where people study for an undergraduate (= first) or postgraduate (= higher level ) degree :
a place of higher education usually for people who have finished twelve years of schooling and where they can obtain more knowledge and skills , and get a degree to recognize this:
examples: Which university did you go to (= did you study at)
Which university were you at (= did you study at)
Most students who attend university find it a rewarding and enjoyable experience .
She teaches at the University of Connecticut.
I graduated from Liverpool University in 2012.
A new arts centre is being built on the university campus .

definitions: being the only existing one of its type or, more generally , unusual , or special in some way:
being the only existing one of its type or, more generally , unusual or special in some way:
something that is unique is unusual or the only one of its type :
a unique problem , challenge , etc. is difficult to deal with because it has never happened before:
if something is unique to a place or situation , it only exists in that place or situation :
examples: Each person's genetic code is unique except in the case of identical twins .
I'd recognize your handwriting anywhere - it's unique.
Do not miss this unique opportunity to buy all six pans at half the recommended price .
As many as 100 species of fish , some unique to
Each person’s DNA is unique.
He's uniquely qualified to run this agency .

definitions: knowledge about a subject , situation , etc. or about how something works :
a particular way in which something is understood , or a particular piece of knowledge :
a positive relationship between two people or groups in which they feel sympathy for each other:
an informal agreement between people :
If you do something on the understanding that something else can or will happen , you do it because someone else has promised that it can or will:
examples: She doesn't have any understanding of politics / human nature /what it takes to be a good manager .
My understanding of the agreement (= what I think it means )
The Supreme Court has radically revised previous understandings of the Constitution.
Students work on applications or interpretations of the material to develop new or deeper understandings of a given topic .
For peace to exist in the region there needs to be a much improved understanding between all the parties concerned .
It took several hours of discussion before they could come to an understanding.

definitions: in the way that most often happens :
examples: He usually gets home about six o'clock.
I usually just have a sandwich for lunch .
Is your friend usually so rude ?
Usually we go skiing in February .
"Do you cook your own meals in the evenings ?" "Usually."

a place of higher education usually for people who have finished twelve years of schooling and where they can obtain more knowledge and skills , and get a degree to recognize this:
examples: Which university did you go to (= did you study at)
Which university were you at (= did you study at)
Most students who attend university find it a rewarding and enjoyable experience .
She teaches at the University of Connecticut.
I graduated from Liverpool University in 2012.
A new arts centre is being built on the university campus .

definitions: to be something that someone will experience or have to deal with soon :
Upon can be used to show that something happens soon after, and often because of, something else :
examples: Upon her head she wore a black velvet hat .
You can never place enough emphasis upon the importance of safety .
Upon your arrival (= as soon as you arrive )
Another few weeks and spring will be upon us.
That depends upon the circumstances .
She insisted upon knowing the truth .
